title: Handwashing Side by Side
description: The RGM watches the employee wash their hands and fills in the checklist, without coaching until the end. Then the knowledge check. This has to be 100% before going back to work.

questions.title: Did the employee wet their hands under warm running water?
questions.explanation: Warm running water first, before the soap goes on.

questions.title: Was approved antibacterial soap applied?
questions.explanation: The approved soap from the dispenser. Not dish soap, not whatever is nearest.

questions.title: Did the employee lather their hands for at least 20 seconds, including wrists, backs of hands, between fingers and under fingernails?
questions.explanation: 20 seconds, and all of it — wrists, backs, between the fingers and under the nails. Under the nails is the one that gets skipped.

questions.title: Was the soap rinsed off using warm running water?
questions.explanation: All the soap off, under warm running water.

questions.title: Did the employee use a single-use paper towel to dry their hands?
questions.explanation: A paper towel, used once. Never an apron, a uniform or a cloth towel.

questions.title: Did the employee turn off the faucet using a paper towel?
questions.explanation: With the towel. They turned that faucet on with dirty hands.

questions.title: Did the employee apply approved hand sanitizer after drying their hands?
questions.explanation: Sanitizer goes on last, on dry hands. On wet hands it is watered down.

questions.title: You must wash your hands when you arrive at work.
questions.explanation: First thing, every shift, before you touch anything.

questions.title: You must wash your hands before putting on gloves and each time you change gloves.
questions.explanation: Every time. A clean glove over a dirty hand is still a dirty hand.

questions.title: Hand sanitizer can replace handwashing if you are busy.
questions.explanation: Never, however busy it gets. Sanitizer goes on after washing, not instead of it.

questions.title: After touching your face, hair, apron, glasses, or cell phone, handwashing is required.
questions.explanation: All of them, and the phone is the one people forget.

questions.title: After using the restroom, you only need to wash your hands once.
questions.explanation: Twice. Once before you leave the restroom, then again at the back hand sink — you touched the door on the way out.

questions.title: You must wash your hands after handling money, trash, or dirty dishes.
questions.explanation: All three. Money has been everywhere before it got to you.

questions.title: It is acceptable to dry your hands on your apron if paper towels are unavailable.
questions.explanation: No. If there are no paper towels, that is the problem to fix — an apron undoes the whole wash.
